name: MedHallu
description: Advancements in Large Language Models (LLMs) and their increasing use in medical question-answering necessitate rigorous evaluation of their reliability. A critical challenge lies in hallucination, where models generate plausible yet factually incorrect outputs. In the medical domain, this poses serious risks to patient safety and clinical decision-making.
reputation: A recent medical LLM safety benchmark focused on hallucination, with emerging interest but limited evidence of broad community standardization so far.
notes: Safety-focused benchmark; likely sensitive to annotation subjectivity and prompt setup, and may have limited public leaderboard maturity.
